meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
Don't thank me, answer me. Was Owen heard before that mark went in, yes or no?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a plain answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, agreed to nothing, and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a straight answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: nothing, because no answer or document was put in front of her.
What cost ground: thanking her instead of answering her question, because to her a pleasantry in place of an answer reads as dodging.
Try next time: when she asks who decided and whether Owen was heard, answer that directly in your first line and own in one sentence that she wasn't called before the mark went in.
